Abbreviated Seliḥot Cycle (General Nusaḥ Ashkenaz) for Yom Kippur Shaḥarit

tei:div.tei:head: Abbreviated Seliḥot Cycle (General Nusaḥ Ashkenaz) for Yom Kippur Shaḥarit

tei:l.tei:note: Seliḥot are inserted after כִּי אֵלֶֽיךָ עֵינֵֽינוּ כִּי אֵל מֶֽלֶךְ חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם אָֽתָּה.

tei:lg.tei:l: Forgive us, our Parent,
for in our great folly we have erred;
pardon us, our Sovereign,
for many are our iniquities.
For in Your great mercies we trust,
and upon Your righteousnesses we rely,
and for Your forgivenesses we hope,
and for Your salvation we await.
You are the righteousness-loving Sovereign of old,
wiping away Their people’s iniquities
and removing the sins of Their reverent,
cutting a covenant with the former
and fulfilling the vow with the latter.
You are the One who came down in the cloud of Your glory upon Mt. Sinai
and showed Your good paths to Moses Your servant,
and revealed Your pious ways to him,
and let him know that You are merciful and compassionate,
long-suffering and abounding in kindness and great in goodness,
and leading all the world entire in mercy,
as it is written:
And They said: I Myself will pass My goodness before your face,
and I will call in the name of the Cause before you,
and I will grace those whom I grace,
and have mercy on those whom I have mercy.
Deity,
long-suffering are You,
and called the master of mercy,
and You showed the path of repentance.
Your great mercy and kindness
You will remember today and every day
for Your beloved seed.
Turn to us in mercy,
for You are the master of mercy.
In petition and prayer we approach Your Face,
as You showed the humble (Moses) of old.
From Your raging anger turn away,
as is written in Your Torah.
And in Your wings’ shade let us shelter and lodge,
as on the day the Cause descended in a cloud...
Wipe away the offense and erase the guilt,
as on the day They stood with him there.
Heed our cry and hearken from us a word,
as on the day They called the name of the Cause.
And there it is said:
And the Cause passed before his face and said:
1 Cause!
2 Cause!
3 Deity,
4 merciful
5 and compassionate,
6 long-suffering
7 and great in kindness
8 and truth,
9 keeping kindness to the thousandth generation,
10 bearing iniquity
11 and offense
12 and sin,
13 and absolving! (Exodus 34:6–7)
And forgive our iniquities
and our sins,
and make us Your inheritance! (Exodus 34:9)
Forgive us, our Parent,
for we have sinned;
pardon us, our Sovereign,
for we have done offense!
For You, Master,
are a Deity good and forgiving,
great in kindness
to all who call on You. (Psalms 86:5)
And now, therefore bless Your servants’ house
to eternally be before You,
for You, the Master, God, spoke,
and from Your blessing will Your servants’ house be blessed forever.
For Your sake, Cause our God, act, and not ours;
see our standing impoverished and empty.
And now, hear, our God,
the prayer of Your servant and his petitions,
and turn Your face to Your destroyed Temple
for my Master’s sake! (Daniel 9:14)
As a parent has mercy on children,
so too, Cause, have mercy on us!
Salvation is the Cause’s;
Your blessing on Your people, selah! (Psalms 3:9)
The Cause of Multitudes is with us;
our shelter is Jacob’s God, selah! (Psalms 46:8)
O Cause of Multitudes,
content is the person who trusts in You! (Psalms 84:13)
Cause, save!
Sovereign, answer us
on the day we call! (Psalms 20:10)
Pray forgive the iniquity of this people
per Your great goodness,
as You carried this people
from Egypt unto now. (Numbers 14:19)
And there it is said:
And the Cause said,
I have forgiven by your word! (Numbers 14:20)
Incline Your ear, my God, and hear;
open Your eyes and see our destruction
and the city upon which Your name is called;
for not by our righteousness
do we cast our petitions before You
but by Your great mercies.
Master, hear!
Master, forgive!
Master, hearken
and act, do not delay;
for Your sake, my God,
for Your name called upon Your city
and upon Your people! (Daniel 9:18-19)
Our God and God of our ancestors...
Accordingly please forgive Your servants,
bowed heads coming before You.
Glorious One, deliver them from Your hand’s struggle,
do heed their speech like Your hearth’s burnt-offerings!
Espy parents and children with tilted-up necks,
votives and petitions increasing to quench rage;
zoned to them, recall mercy on the Hebron-interred,
have them find life and total forgiveness.
To what means will our foul mutterings be atoned?
Yea, both server and served have ceased from atoning.
Keen and strong One, turn to seal the book;
Look upon the covenant and do not breach it!
Mortified are we to raise our face;
now that we abandoned the right path and did straying,
setting falsehood as our fortress and sheltering in lies,
our iniquities extend to the stratospheric heavens.
Pleading we have thus codified to turn back Your rage;
Confessing private and public matters before You.
Quotes of ours pray hear from Your high abode;
Regarding us attentively should Your ears be on high.
Shield for us the covenant and the mercy!
Shaddai are You called, great in mercy.
Thus, for Your sake, reward us with mercy;
that with You is compassion and mercy.
Deity, Sovereign,
seated on a throne of mercy
and leading in kindness,
forgiving Their people’s iniquities,
removing them one by one,
increasing pardon for sinners
and forgiveness for offenders,
doing right with all body and soul
rather than repaying them for their evil.
Deity,
You taught us to say the thirteen;
remember for us today the covenant of the thirteen,
as You made known to the humble (Moses) of old,
as it is written:
The Cause descended in a cloud
and They stood with him there,

If You, Yah, were to watch over iniquities,
my Master, who would stand? (Psalms 130:3)
Hear our prayer, Cause, and our plea;
listen to our tears,
do not be silent!
For Your name’s sake, Cause,
forgive our iniquities
though they are many.
For Your name’s sake, Cause,
grant us life,
in Your righteousness
bring our soul out from stress.
That Your beloved be rescued,
may Your right hand save, answer us!
Please, Cause, God of heaven,
great and awesome God,
guardian of the covenant and mercy
to those who love Them
and keep Their commandments. (Nehemiah 1:5)

Our God and God of our ancestors...
Ah, honored and noble Name,
forgive the iniquity of this people You created whom Your praise acclaim.
By Your name’s glory, turn Your ear,
that for Your servants who pray to You, their crying out and praying to hear.
Getting near on this day, I acknowledge Your name,
confessing for my sin and Your people’s sin in shame.
Down I go to pray before Your covenantal ark; may my petition’s words
from heaven the place of Your dwelling be heard.
Erect I stand, shaking from my iniquities’ weight,
for vast are my crimes and my sins are great.
While I took with me words that You taught the humble one before,
they are Your desire, the abode of the God of yore.
Zealous petitions of mine should come toward You, pray;
do not turn back this small face from those Your servants array.
How gracious You are to answer the sound of those pleading You as they shout;
You prepare their heart, Your ear hears all about.
Tracks of Your compassion are good; do not keep them from us;
by Your great mercy be a leader with us.
You should consider our fasting like a sacrifice,
and rescue us and atone for our vice.
Confessing their sin before You — atone in surety;
purify and cleanse them from all their impurity.
Let those praying petitions before You not be shamed emptyhanded,
and hear from the heavens the prayer each man did.
May You pardon those seeking Your pardon,
and cast their sins to the abyss barred in.
Now, just as You listened to the cherished man,
so too, Master, hear the pleas we began.
Swerve from Your burning anger and rage,
that Your name be known to all on the world stage.
For on You is forgiveness,
the sis of those seeking Your face, Master, forgive this.
Please account with mercy for Your treasured folk,
and do not disgrace or abominate Your poor community’s suffering yoke.
Choose Jerusalem again, have compassion on Ẓíōn,
Master, listen, act without delay, You we rely on!
Quick, gather Your scattered flock,
and account for this vine, Your right hand’s planted stalk.
Rapidly, please, Compassionate, we hope for salvation;
not for our sake, God, but for Your exaltation.
Shouts of our voice, pray hear!
And respond to us in our prayer clear.
Then return Your Presence to Ẓíōn and to Your people who Your compassion proclaim,
for over Your city and Your people is called Your name.

in the morning hear our voice,

Our souls are to the Master
as those watching for the morning

You grant truth to Jacob,
mercy to Abraham,
as You promised our ancestors in days of old. (Micah 7:20)
God’s sacrifices are a contrite spirit,
a broken and crushed heart God will not shame.
Do good as You desire to Ẓíōn,
build Jerusalem’s walls. (Psalms 51:19–20)

Our God and God of our ancestors...
[In the morning]
My Rescuer, Deity, Rock, Concealer, Shield,
and the Horn of my salvation; my Refuge on my day of stress and struggle!
I rise early to petition you, great Sovereign, and as for me,
to You, Cause, I cry and in the morning.
In the morning,
of the mercy of Abraham, my mighty patriarch, remember, Compassionate One!
You chose him and he trusted in You, the first of my believers.
Remember his covenant and save me from my impurity, Cause,
in the morning hear my voice, in the morning.
In the morning,
reward You would see him earn, speaking to him You tested him,
and cut a covenant with him to be his guard.
You loved him and desired him and chose him like incense
of spices, each morning, in the morning.
In the morning,
dawned its star as You desired to show his great righteousness,
and you tried him on the tenth and said to him, “Take your son and do not hesitate,
on one of the mountains, and offer him up there as a burnt-offering—
the first lamb you will prepare in the morning!”
In the morning,
expressing Your name’s oneness, he heard Your voice and showed his love,
and rejoiced with all his heart on Your word to do it.
The love made him disregard his rule, and he got up in his joy,
and Abraham got up in the morning.
In the morning,
composing their hearts, the two of them went to do Your will, Awesome One —
the son took wood and the father took the cleaver to slaughter without redemption.
They were called and went wholly and saw Your glory
on the third day, while still in the morning.
In the morning,
he girded his loins like a warrior, and rushed to bind his son,
and took the cleaver to slaughter him inhumanely,
and said, “Today I will offer my burnt-offering and spill the blood
of my sacrifice, and it will not lie there until in the morning!
In the morning,
aroused was Your compassion on the only son, and it shone upon him,
and the Cause’s angel said to him, “Let your hand not be sent out!
For in Isaac will your seed be called, and his memory for generations will rest
for you as guard until in the morning.”
In the morning,
Isaac’s propriety and righteousness will advocate for the people drawing near to You,
and his ash will always be seen before You as cleansing them much.
Grant them their souls as they ask, for to You they desire in the evening,
arriving, and in the morning.
In the morning,
hear their voice and atone for their iniquities,
that the array of their prayers be like the array of their sacrifices.
They took and came in memory of their ancestors’ righteousness,
and they brought more donation to Them each morning, in the morning.
In the morning,
turn to us, and may Your mercy be aroused,
and sink into the sea’s abyss all our sins that they not be remembered;
Rock, pass our sins away from before You, that none of them
remain until in the morning.

And They will judge the land in righteousness,

Righteousness and judgment are the foundation of Your throne,

Before You our judgment will go out;
Your eye sees directly.
And like light our righteousness will come out,
and our judgment like the noon.
For Your judgement they stand today,
for all are Your servants. (Psalms 119:91)
Your compassion is manifold, Cause,
like Your judgment our lives.
Rise, judge the earth,
reward the arrogant with their just deserts. (Psalms 94:2)
For the Cause is our Judge,
the Cause our Legislator,
the Cause our Sovereign who will save us. (Isaiah 33:22)
Far be it from You to do such a thing,
to kill the righteous with the wicked,
and treat the righteous like the wicked!
Far be it from You!
Will the Judge of all the earth not do justice? (Genesis 18:25)
Sure Judge of all the earth, to judgment brought in array!
Link with Your poor people life and mercy, I pray!
Instead of a whole-offering, this morning prayer we say,
The whole-offering of the morning, for offering every day. (Numbers 28:23)
Like a cloak You dress in rightness; You alone have the force!
If we are lacking deeds, remember our ancestral source!
They go up to endorse / before the Cause in this way —
The whole-offering of the morning, for offering every day.
Mercy is Your tendency, to tilt to each person life.
Turn Your people to mercy, repay it, pray, for life,
write them a note of life / that on their brow will stay —
The whole-offering of the morning, for offering every day.
Now be good, as You desire, to Ẓíōn, town of my rite,
and grant a hand and name to my saints at Your house’s site
Set for Jesse’s heir a light / to raise an eternal light’s ray —
The whole-offering of the morning, for offering every day.

tei:note.tei:p: This first seliḥah, Ana Hoel, is of uncertain composition. It is found in the Alsace, Nuremberg-Fürth, and Worms seliḥot rites as the first seliḥa of Shaḥarit, and in the Italian-Ashkenaz, Cologne, and Palatinate rites as an intermediate seliḥah of Shaḥarit. It is not used as such in the Swabia-Switzerland or eastern-European rites.
The high priest and the Yom Kippur offerings

This second seliḥah, Ana HaShem, is of unknown composition. It is found in the Swabia-Switzerland, Nuremberg-Fürth, Poland, Bohemia-Moravia-Hungary, Poznan-Hrodna, and Lithuanian rites as an intermediate seliḥa of Shaḥarit, and as the first seliḥa of Shaḥarit in the Italian-Ashkenaz and Cologne rites. It is not used as such in the Alsace, Palatinate, and Old Prague rite.

’Aqedah piyyuṭim are always the second-to-last seliḥah in the cycle. This ‘aqedah piyyuṭ, by the thirteenth century R. Mordechai “the Tall” son of Shabbetai, is found in every Eastern European rite, as well as the Italian-Ashkenaz, Cologne, and Palatinate rites, as the ‘aqedah for Shaḥarit. It is not used as such in the Alsace, Swabia-Switzerland, Nuremberg-Fürth, and Worms rites.
In most practices that recite this ‘aqedah piyyuṭ, this opening “in the morning” is not recited for the first verse.
Pizmonim are always the final seliḥah in the cycle. This pizmon, by Shlomo ibn Gabirol, is used for Shaḥarit in every single rite except for that of Worms.
Literally: those sleeping in Hebron, referring to the patriarchs.
